title: PARTROOT196-EH28-T2: exact 2/sqrt3 sieve with the byte-maximal 28-step ladder envelope and heralded tolerance 1 - 1/((16*10^126-1)(625*10^126-1))

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single PARTROOT196 algorithm and configuration of proof.md and virtual.md (finite streaming tester with n+10 shifted X-tests per candidate for n < 2^512; for n >= 2^512, z0 = min{j: 3j^2 >= n}, z = z0 + 16 ceil(log2 n), ell = m = dl = z, growing odd-partition k = least odd >= ceil(n^(1/8)), rolling backward C_i, Y = ceil(log2 C0), u = max(Y, 2z) + 2, Qcap = 4nC0 + K, and the fully counted physical bank of proof.md), with every source acquisition served by FILTER of heralded.md H.2 (handed-over cap Q* = N(n+10) for n < 2^512 and Qcap otherwise, raw cutoff D Q* with D = (16*10^126 - 1)(625*10^126 - 1); it hands every copy over when copies carry no herald) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-7 from independent ideal copies and under every adversary of the heralded malformed-copy model of claim 4 (heralded.md Lemmas H.1-H.2, Theorem H.3). On EVERY execution branch, including every failure, discard, retry, partial attempt and abort, its total charged sequential work satisfies T = O(E(n)) by the explicit common bound C*2^((2/sqrt3) sqrt n + 512 n^(7/16)) proved in virtual.md 15.1 and proof.md 8-10, which heralded.md Theorem H.3 preserves with an absolute constant when all raw acquisitions, herald reads, resets and counter steps of FILTER are counted, and the absorption Lemma E.3 with E.4 of envelope.md, with E(n) = 2^(a sqrt(n) - M sum_{i=1..27} n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(M+1-i)) - M2 n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(M-27))), where M = 10^256 - 1, M2 is DEFINED as the positive integer whose decimal digits are the coefficient of the last structured exponent term without its minus sign (an all-nines integer with fewer digits than M, so 1 <= M2 <= M; the proof uses only this inequality, never its digit count) and a = P/Q is the exact rational of envelope.md E.1 (256-digit P and Q with 3P^2 - 4Q^2 = 3, so a > 2/sqrt3); E is exactly the structured bound (29 exponent terms: the leading term, 27 ladder terms with coefficient -M, one last ladder term with coefficient -M2; outer nPower 0 and outer logPower 0). The growth index of E is exactly 1/2 (envelope.md E.2). These four resource bounds hold jointly for this one algorithm and configuration, together with the tolerance claim.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single PARTROOT196 algorithm and configuration of proof.md and virtual.md (finite streaming tester with n+10 shifted X-tests per candidate for n < 2^512; for n >= 2^512, z0 = min{j: 3j^2 >= n}, z = z0 + 16 ceil(log2 n), ell = m = dl = z, growing odd-partition k = least odd >= ceil(n^(1/8)), rolling backward C_i, Y = ceil(log2 C0), u = max(Y, 2z) + 2, Qcap = 4nC0 + K, and the fully counted physical bank of proof.md), with every source acquisition served by FILTER of heralded.md H.2 (handed-over cap Q* = N(n+10) for n < 2^512 and Qcap otherwise, raw cutoff D Q* with D = (16*10^126 - 1)(625*10^126 - 1); it hands every copy over when copies carry no herald) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-7 from independent ideal copies and under every adversary of the heralded malformed-copy model of claim 4 (heralded.md Lemmas H.1-H.2, Theorem H.3). On EVERY execution branch, including every failure, discard, retry, partial attempt and abort, its peak allocated classical bits satisfy S_C = O(n) (proof.md 8; FILTER adds two O(n)-bit counters and one herald bit, heralded.md Theorem H.3). The envelope B_C(n) = n has growth index exactly 0. These four resource bounds hold jointly for this one algorithm and configuration, together with the tolerance claim.

The growth index of E is exactly 1/2. These four resource bounds hold jointly for this one algorithm and configuration, together with the tolerance claim.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single PARTROOT196 algorithm and configuration of proof.md and virtual.md (finite streaming tester with n+10 shifted X-tests per candidate for n < 2^512; for n >= 2^512, z0 = min{j: 3j^2 >= n}, z = z0 + 16 ceil(log2 n), ell = m = dl = z, growing odd-partition k = least odd >= ceil(n^(1/8)), rolling backward C_i, Y = ceil(log2 C0), u = max(Y, 2z) + 2, Qcap = 4nC0 + K, and the fully counted physical bank of proof.md), with every source acquisition served by FILTER of heralded.md H.2 (handed-over cap Q* = N(n+10) for n < 2^512 and Qcap otherwise, raw cutoff D Q* with D = (16*10^126 - 1)(625*10^126 - 1); it hands every copy over when copies carry no herald) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-7 from independent ideal copies and under every adversary of the heralded malformed-copy model of claim 4 (heralded.md Lemmas H.1-H.2, Theorem H.3). On EVERY execution branch, including every failure, discard, retry, partial attempt and abort, the total number Q of source copies acquired, counting every raw copy acquired by FILTER (malformed ones included) and every discarded or failed-attempt copy, satisfies Q = O(E(n)) by the explicit common bound C*2^((2/sqrt3) sqrt n + 512 n^(7/16)) proved in virtual.md 15.1 and proof.md 8-10, which heralded.md Theorem H.3 preserves with an absolute constant when all raw acquisitions, herald reads, resets and counter steps of FILTER are counted, and the absorption Lemma E.3 with E.4 of envelope.md, with the same E(n): E(n) = 2^(a sqrt(n) - M sum_{i=1..27} n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(M+1-i)) - M2 n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(M-27))), where M = 10^256 - 1, M2 is DEFINED as the positive integer whose decimal digits are the coefficient of the last structured exponent term without its minus sign (an all-nines integer with fewer digits than M, so 1 <= M2 <= M; the proof uses only this inequality, never its digit count) and a = P/Q is the exact rational of envelope.md E.1 (256-digit P and Q with 3P^2 - 4Q^2 = 3, so a > 2/sqrt3); E is exactly the structured bound (29 exponent terms: the leading term, 27 ladder terms with coefficient -M, one last ladder term with coefficient -M2; outer nPower 0 and outer logPower 0). The growth index of E is exactly 1/2. These four resource bounds hold jointly for this one algorithm and configuration, together with the tolerance claim.

For the same algorithm and configuration (PARTROOT196 with FILTER), the proved fractional tolerance is epsilon(n) = 1 - 1/D with D = (16*10^126 - 1)(625*10^126 - 1) = 10^256 - 641*10^126 + 1, a constant in (0,1), written as the product expression of heralded.md H.6 (numerator 10^126 (10^130 - 641) = D - 1, denominator (16*10^126 - 1)(625*10^126 - 1) = D, each displayed factor at most 64 digits). Under the heralded malformed-copy model of heralded.md H.1 (structured error_model text): if Q copies are acquired on a branch, at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of them are malformed, the herald is always correct, and the adversary chooses adaptively which copies are malformed and their arbitrary (possibly entangled) contents. For every N >= 2 and s, the algorithm recovers the entire s with probability at least 1 - 2^-7 > 2/3 under every such adversary, jointly with the four resource bounds above, which count all raw acquisitions (heralded.md Lemmas H.1-H.2 and Theorem H.3). This covers detectable (heralded) malformed copies only; no tolerance of undetectable corruption is claimed. The clean problem (no herald, all copies ideal) is also solved with the same bounds.

structured.error_model: Heralded malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires on an execution branch, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Each acquired copy consists of an (n+1)-qubit register of the ideal copy's shape together with one classical herald bit f delivered with it. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed. A well-formed copy has f = 0 and its register is a fresh copy of rho_s, in tensor product with every other system (earlier copies, the adversary's system and the algorithm's registers). A malformed copy has f = 1 and its register is in an arbitrary state chosen by the adversary, possibly entangled with the adversary's private system and with other malformed copies. On every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. The herald is always correct, so malformation is detectable (an erasure-type error); its timing, its number within the promise and the malformed register contents are adversarial. In the clean problem no herald is supplied and every copy is well-formed. No source control, purification access or preparation inverse is supplied.
